newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS - France, Germany vow no delay to EMU.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - France, Germany vow no delay to EMU.

text.p: France and Germany, leaders in the drive to monetary union, vowed on Wednesday that there would be no delay to plans to launch a single European currency in January 1999.

"The timetable for Economic and Monetary Union will be respected. I have no doubt about that," French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told a news conference after a meeting with German Finance Minister Theo Waigel and the central bank heads of France and Germany.

"There is no reason to talk about the timetable. Germany is trying to meet the (Maastricht) criteria and let's see what the result is," Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer told Reuters Financial Television.

The meeting, part of a regular series between Europe's two biggest economies, took place amid resurgent speculation that EMU might be delayed to give Germany more time to meet Maastricht treaty criteria.

Private economists say they doubt whether Germany, meant to be Europe's model economy, can reduce its budget deficit to three percent of gross domestic product this year, in line with Maastricht treaty requirements.
Arthuis said however he was confident both France and Germany would be ready for monetary union.
